key_insight: Instead of optimizing one harness along a fixed path, the paper grows multiple self-improving branches with evolving development sets and proposal policies, then routes each input to the most suitable branch head.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more robust way to tune agent harnesses for math reasoning and coding, reducing local-optimum drift and improving deployment by selecting among complementary specialists.
method: Split search into branches with different evolving development subsets.
Keep cases solved by more of a branch’s leading harnesses and drop universally solved cases.
Use branch-specific search histories to revise proposal policies, then add a router that selects one branch head per new input.
evidence_signal: Using only development data for harness selection and routing, the system reports relative gains over Meta-Harness of 34.8% on Olympiad-level math reasoning, 11.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, and 3.8% on SWE-bench Lite.
watch_item: Performance depends on a development-driven router and branch management, so gains may be sensitive to how branches, selection rules, and search histories are constructed.
paper_title: Mixture of Self-Improving Branches For Agent Harness Optimization
